newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos get his Mitterrands mixed up.
newsitem.headline: Ramos get his Mitterrands mixed up.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos, popularly known as "Steady Eddie" for his coolness under fire, cracked just a bit on Saturday.
In a gaffe that titillated Manila's rambunctious press, he mistakenly referred to the widow of late French President Francois Mitterrand as having died.

"Why would we (ban) the French first lady, Danielle Mitterrand, who died already," Ramos asked reporters in southern Davao city, denying Manila newspaper reports that the government had a list of 100 foreigners barred from the country during next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit.
"I should know. I wrote a letter of condolences to President Mitterrand," Ramos added, apparently referring to condolences he sent Mrs Mitterrand when her husband died of cancer in January.
"Oops! Ramos 'kills' wrong Mitterrand," a headline in the Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper said.
The Malaya (Free) daily said in its headline: "Danielle Mitterrand is alive and well, thank you."
